mentions.text: Hey HN, I built* HIIT Builder ( https://hiitbuilder.app ) because I don't want to get fat. Truly I could just stop there. But for more context, I got tired of hunting for YouTube workout videos that have both good routines and decent music. Turns out most YT workout creators, even the massive ones who could afford a license, have terrible music. So, fk it, I'll build my own workout generator and play my own Spotify playlists instead. So far workouts have been completed across 13 countries (US, Iraq, Bangladesh, Austria, France, Germany, Brazil, Ukraine, Turkey, Netherlands, Spain, Chile, Australia), and someone in the Faroe Islands, either physically or maybe just their VPN, started one too. A few technical details that might be interesting to my fellow nerds here: After a few ugly first prototypes for the stick figures, I ended up using the strategy of modeling every animation as a compact 34-number pose vector (joint angles, abduction, etc.) like a 3D skeleton, then projecting it to a 2D SVG. Why do you still believe it? [1]: They (claim to) take 45% of ad placement sales, so not including revenue from selling trends/user data. mentions.text: Almost everyone will say they're huge music fans, enjoying music is probably one of the most common shared human experiences. But in there are vastly different levels of how "into it" people really are. Now obviously this is true for a lot of things, where there are casual fans and people who are more into it as a serious hobby. But for music there is a significant amount of people who will say that they're huge music fans that in reality have extremely shallow knowledge of the music scene, even of the artist that they're fans of. "I'm a huge country fan Chris Stapleton is my favorite singer" you ask what they thought of his latest album from the other year and get back a " Oh I don't know but Tennessee Whiskey is my favorite song." It's the people who used to mostly just put on top 40 radio, who now probably just have 5 or 6 spotify or youtube algorithm curated playlists saved that they listen on repeat. Now, I don't mean to invalidate people's experience and I don't want to push some elitist takes on "being a real music fan". It's perfectly fine to listen to music without making it an active hobby.
